overview: Slovenia is a small country in Central Europe, between the Alps and the Adriatic Sea. Its capital is Ljubljana. Slovenia was the first republic to leave Yugoslavia, declaring independence in 1991. It joined the European Union and NATO in 2004, and in 2007 it became the first former communist country to adopt the euro.

geography.text: More than half of Slovenia is covered by forest. The Julian Alps rise in the north-west, including Triglav, the highest peak, which appears on the national flag. The south-west is karst country, with limestone caves such as Postojna and Škocjan. Slovenia's Adriatic coastline is less than 50 kilometres long.

history.text: Slovenes settled the eastern Alps in the 500s and were ruled for centuries by the Habsburgs. Slovenia joined the new Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes in 1918, which later became Yugoslavia. In 1991 it declared independence and won it after a war that lasted just ten days.

events.title: First Slovene book
events.text: Primož Trubar publishes the first books in the Slovene language.

events.title: A new South Slav state
events.text: Slovenia joins the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes.

events.title: The Ten-Day War
events.text: Slovenia declares independence and wins a short war against the Yugoslav army.

events.title: Joins the EU and NATO
events.text: Slovenia becomes a member of both.

events.title: Adopts the euro
events.text: Slovenia is the first former communist country to use the euro.

government.text: Slovenia is a parliamentary republic. The National Assembly chooses the Prime Minister, and the President is elected directly every five years. Slovenia joined NATO and the European Union in 2004 and was the first former communist country to adopt the euro, in 2007.

economy.text: Slovenia is the richest of the former Yugoslav republics. It exports cars, medicines, electrical appliances and machinery, and the port of Koper is a key gateway to central Europe. More than half the country is covered in forest.

culture.text: Slovenia's landscape packs Alps, lakes, caves and a short stretch of coast into a small country. Lake Bled, with its island church, is one of Europe's most photographed places. Beekeeping is a national tradition, and Slovenia's native bee is protected.

items.title: Lake Bled
items.text: A lake with a tiny island church and a castle on a cliff.

items.title: Postojna Cave
items.text: A cave system with a railway running inside it.

items.title: Beekeeping
items.text: Slovenia proposed World Bee Day, held every 20 May.

sport.text: Slovenia punches far above its weight in sport. Tadej Pogačar and Primož Roglič are among the world's best cyclists, Luka Dončić is an NBA star, and Janja Garnbret is the world's leading sport climber.

items.title: Tadej Pogačar
items.text: Won the Tour de France in 2020, 2021, 2024 and 2025.

items.title: Janja Garnbret
items.text: Olympic sport climbing champion in 2021 and 2024.

items.title: Luka Dončić
items.text: One of the NBA's leading scorers.

didYouKnow: Slovenia is one of the most forested countries in Europe; about 58% is covered in trees.
Melania Trump, a former First Lady of the United States, was born in Slovenia.
